evidence.source: 國學大全 字形演變
evidence.text: Lists 忘 forms in a late Spring-and-Autumn bronze inscription, Warring States writing, seal, clerical and regular scripts; names examples including 蔡侯紐鐘 and several Warring States bronzes. Its account says from bronze through regular script the graph is 心 plus 亡, with 心 semantic and 亡 phonetic. This is a secondary paleographic summary; it establishes neither an oracle-bone form nor the earliest occurrence.
evidence.title: 忘字形演变字源

evidence.text: The exact file page describes 忘-seal.svg as a vector drawing of 忘 in Shuowen seal-script style, points to source image S07737 on hanziyuan.net, and gives a public-domain release for the SVG representation. It is a modern digital redraw, not an artifact photograph. The page also lists Shang oracle and bronze variants, but they were not selected because their direct file links could not be retrieved successfully.

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstructions, Middle Chinese reading and component analysis
evidence.text: The entry labels 忘 a phonosemantic compound with phonetic 亡 and semantic 心. In Baxter–Sagart 2014 it gives 忘 *maŋ and *maŋ-s, with Middle Chinese mjang and mjangH; its Zhengzhang section identifies 亡 as the phonetic component and gives 忘 *maŋ and *maŋs. These are reconstructions in named systems, not direct evidence for when the graph was formed. The local Baxter–Sagart rows agree: 亡 MC mjang, OC *maŋ; 忘 MC mjang / mjangH, OC *maŋ / *maŋ-s.
evidence.kind: tertiary reconstruction summary checked against local rows
evidence.title: 忘 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: Official record for U+5FD8 lists kMandarin wàng, kHanyuPinyin wàng, and the definition “forget; neglect; miss, omit.” This is current reference metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship. The supplied local Unihan rows match: 忘 wàng and 亡 wáng.
evidence.kind: official Unicode character metadata cross-checked against local rows
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+5FD8

evidence.text: An attempt to open the official U+4EA1 record was inaccessible through the web tool. The supplied local Unihan exact row gives 亡 wáng; the local row is not external evidence and Unihan pronunciation metadata does not establish a historical phonetic role.

evidence.text: The dossier records the Shuowen gloss 不識也 and analysis 从心从亡，亡亦聲 (“not to recognize/know”; composed of 心 and 亡, with 亡 also phonetic). This is a Han lexicographic account, not proof of the graph’s earliest formation. The CText page could not be opened in this run, so this remains dossier evidence rather than newly verified page content.

search_audit.outcome: One initial search call combined four distinct queries. Opened the paleographic summary, Commons file page and Wiktionary entry. MOE page open failed; primary inscription image links on the paleographic page returned cache misses. Follow-up opened official Unihan U+5FD8 successfully and attempted U+4EA1, which remained inaccessible. Commons’ exact original file URL was obtained from its description page; fetching the image itself failed.
Opened and inspected; verified current kMandarin wàng.
Open attempt failed in the web tool. Local exact reading row was available but is not external evidence.

gaps: No securely dated oracle-bone example or Shang-era attestation was verified. The accessible paleographic page records later bronze examples, beginning with a late Spring-and-Autumn example, and later script forms; its links to individual inscriptions returned cache misses.

No dated early textual use or documented chronology of semantic extensions such as ‘forget’, ‘neglect’, ‘miss’, and ‘omit’ was established. A lexicographic gloss and current dictionary definitions do not by themselves provide semantic chronology.

No primary inscription image could be opened to examine strokes, variants, or possible graphic corruption. The accessible account supports a 心 semantic plus 亡 phonetic analysis in the listed bronze-to-later forms, but gives no competing corruption theory.

The local Baxter–Sagart rows support a same-system comparison: 亡 *maŋ and 忘 *maŋ / *maŋ-s, with MC mjang versus mjang / mjangH. The secondary entry also names the phonetic role. This does not date the compound or prove a specific historical sound change. Current Mandarin rows are 亡 wáng and 忘 wàng; only 忘’s official Unihan page was accessible.

The dossier’s suggestion that 忘 derives from 亡 with a perfective suffix remains unverified in this bounded research. No independent early attestations establishing separate source-word and borrowed-word histories were inspected; no whole-graph borrowing account is established here.

The selected seal-script image is a modern vector redraw of a historical script style, not an ancient artifact photograph. Its exact direct image URL is known from the Commons page, but image retrieval failed in this research tool; pixel inspection is left to the downstream image review.
